name: Timur (Tamerlane), Rebuilder of Mongol Power
summary: Timur (Tamerlane), a Turco-Mongol ruler from Samarkand, rebuilds Mongol-scale conquest in the late 14th century. He destroys the Golden Horde (1395-1396), sacks Delhi (1398), defeats the Mamluks in Syria (1400-1401), and destroys the Ottoman army at Ankara (1402). His empire collapses on his death (1405) but the devastation of Persia, Iraq, and Anatolia reshapes these regions for generations.

_quarry.structural_significance: Timur's conquests represent the last great Mongol-style empire; his destruction of the Golden Horde opens the Pontic steppe to Moscow's expansion; his defeat of the Ottomans gives Constantinople 50 more years; his sack of Delhi's Punjab depopulation reduces the basis for another large Muslim empire in India for half a century; unlike the Mongols, Timur is a Muslim, his destruction is done in the name of religious reform, not steppe pragmatism
